column1: # provost secret patterns (PV-028; the start of PV-033's redaction rules)
# What a secret looks like. 'provost --env' records an allow-listed
# environment variable (PROVOST_ENV_VARS) only when no row here matches it:
# a variable whose name or value matches one is never recorded, and its name
# goes to the capture's env.withheld key instead. A row matches by kind of
# leak, not by tool, so a new token format is one new row.
#   kind     a short name for what the pattern finds (shown in the warning)
#   field    name  = the variable's name, upper-cased before matching
#            value = the variable's value, as it is
#   case     i = ignore case, - = match case
#   pattern  a POSIX extended regular expression (Bash [[ =~ ]]), unanchored
#            unless it says ^ or $. Use [[:upper:]], [[:alnum:]] and the like,
#            not A-Z ranges, which depend on the locale.
